title: Chords, arcs, sectors, segments and tangents
keyIdea: A chord is a straight line joining two points on a circle; the diameter is the longest chord, through the centre. An arc is part of the curved edge: the minor arc is less than half, the major arc more. A sector is a region bounded by two radii and an arc; a segment is a region cut off by a chord. A tangent touches the circle at exactly one point, at 90° to the radius there.

kid: Think of a round pizza. The crust all the way round is the circumference. A line from the middle to the crust is a radius.
Draw a straight line from one point on the crust to another. That line is a chord. The longest chord goes through the middle. It is the diameter.
A bit of the curved crust is an arc. Two points split the crust into a short arc and a long arc. The short one is the minor arc. The long one is the major arc.

Cut a slice from the middle, with two straight cuts. That slice is a sector. Make one straight cut across the edge instead. The piece you cut off is a segment. A ruler that just rests against the edge, touching at one spot, is a tangent.
adult: Circles have named parts beyond radius and diameter. A chord is a straight line segment whose two ends lie on the circle. A diameter is a chord that passes through the centre, so it is the longest possible chord, twice the radius.

An arc is part of the circumference between two points. Any two points make two arcs: the minor arc, less than half the circle, and the major arc, more than half. Their angles at the centre add up to 360°, so a 100° minor arc goes with a 260° major arc.

A sector is the region between two radii and the arc joining their ends, shaped like a slice of pizza. A segment is the region between a chord and its arc, with no radii as edges. Each comes in a minor and a major version.

A tangent is a straight line that touches the circle at exactly one point and does not cross it. The radius drawn to that point meets the tangent at 90°. A line that crosses the circle at two points is not a tangent; the part of it inside the circle is a chord. Common mistakes: swapping sector and segment; thinking a diameter is not a chord; choosing the major arc by its position on the page instead of its size; and calling a line that cuts through the circle a tangent.

familyTip: Cut a paper plate or a tortilla. Make one cut from the edge to the middle and back out to make a slice, and one straight cut across the edge. Ask which piece is the sector and which is the segment, and how they know.

worked.title: A and B are points on a circle with centre O, and the minor arc AB is 70°. Name the parts and find the major arc.
steps: The straight line AB joins two points on the circle, so it is a chord. It misses O, so it is not a diameter.
The minor arc AB is the short way round: 70°. The major arc goes the long way: 360° − 70° = 290°.
The region between OA, OB and the minor arc is the minor sector. The region between chord AB and the minor arc is the minor segment.
A tangent at A would touch the circle only at A, at 90° to the radius OA.

practice.prompt: Which of these describes a chord?
choices: A straight line joining two points on the circle
A curved part of the circle's edge
A line from the centre to the edge
practice.hint: A chord is straight, and both of its ends are on the circle.
practice.explain: A chord joins two points on the circle with a straight line. The curved part is an arc, and a centre-to-edge line is a radius.

practice.prompt: A circle has radius {r} cm. How long is the longest chord you can draw in it, in cm?
practice.hint: The longest chord passes through the centre. What is that chord called?
practice.explain: The longest chord is the diameter, which is two radii: 2 × {r} = {=2*r} cm.

practice.prompt: Points A and B split a circle into two arcs. The minor arc AB is {a}°. What is the major arc AB, in degrees?
practice.hint: The two arcs together go all the way round the circle, which is 360°.
practice.explain: The two arcs add up to 360°, so the major arc is 360 − {a} = {=360-a}°.

practice.prompt: A region of a circle is bounded by two radii and an arc. What is it called?
practice.hint: Think of a slice of pizza cut from the middle. Which name goes with two radii?
practice.explain: Two radii and an arc make a sector. A segment is cut off by a chord, and a chord is a line, not a region.

practice.prompt: How many points does a tangent share with its circle?
practice.hint: Picture a ruler resting against a coin. Where do they meet?
practice.explain: A tangent touches the circle at exactly one point. A line meeting it at 2 points cuts through it, and one meeting it at none misses.

choices: Yes: it joins two points on the circle, passing through the centre
No: chords cannot pass through the centre
No: a diameter is an arc
pool.hint: Check the definition of a chord. Does a diameter fit it?
pool.explain: A chord is any straight line joining two points on the circle. A diameter does that, through the centre, so it is the longest chord.

pool.prompt: One straight cut across a round cake, away from the centre, cuts off a small piece. What is that piece?
pool.hint: How many straight edges does the piece have, and are they radii?
pool.explain: The piece is bounded by one chord (the cut) and an arc, so it is a segment. A sector would need two radii.

pool.prompt: The diameter of a circle is {d} cm. How long is its radius, in cm?
pool.hint: A diameter is made of two radii end to end through the centre.
pool.explain: The radius is half the diameter: {d} ÷ 2 = {=d/2} cm.

pool.prompt: OT is a radius and TP is part of the tangent at T. In triangle OTP, angle TOP is {a}°. What is angle OPT, in degrees?
pool.hint: The radius meets the tangent at 90°, so angle OTP is 90°. Then use the angle sum of a triangle.
pool.explain: Angle OTP is 90°. The angles add up to 180°, so angle OPT is 180 − 90 − {a} = {=90-a}°.

pool.prompt: The minor arc AB is 140°. Which statement is true?
choices: The minor arc is the longer of the two
pool.hint: Minor means less than half. The two arcs make a full turn of 360°.
pool.explain: 360° − 140° = 220°, so the major arc is 220°. The minor arc is always the shorter one.

pool.prompt: What is the difference between a sector and a segment?
choices: A sector has two radii as edges; a segment is cut off by a chord
A sector is cut off by a chord; a segment has two radii as edges
pool.hint: Which one looks like a slice of pizza from the middle?
pool.explain: A sector is bounded by two radii and an arc. A segment is bounded by a chord and an arc.

pool.prompt: A straight line cuts a circle at two points. What is the part of the line inside the circle?
pool.hint: Its two ends are on the circle and it is straight.
pool.explain: The inside part joins two points on the circle with a straight line, so it is a chord. A tangent would meet the circle only once.

pool.prompt: A straight line meets a circle at exactly one point and does not cross it. What is the line?
pool.hint: Which line only touches the circle and stays outside it?
pool.explain: That is a tangent. A chord meets the circle at two points, and a radius starts at the centre.

visual.caption: Is each part a line, a region or part of the curved edge? Drag each card, or tap it and then tap a box.

lab.caption: Flagship lab: drag a chord until it becomes a diameter, pick the major arc, find the sector and the segment, and slide a line until it is a tangent.
